answer: Identity is admitted by inbound reachability, not by signature. Each epoch a public lantern picks three independent vantage points; a new key must answer their challenge at its own routable address inside a ninety-second horizon. They record ASN, /24, TLS fingerprint and round-trip, and the registry keeps this as a trellis: one key per branch. Keys sharing branch, fingerprint and latency merge into one operator and are refused. Cloning a thousand agents thus costs a thousand reachable sockets on distinct networks, so a farm rents per identity per round; an honest agent answers three pings.
